item.title: Gallarate: three new exhibitions at the Maga, from Jago to Leopardi
item.description: Starting November 15, 2026, MAGA opens the new season «Jago.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Starting November 15, 2026, MA*GA opens its new season - “Jago. Exposed Bodies” from November 15, 2026 to April 4, 2027 - “Water” at Palazzo Lombardia from November 11, 2026 - “According to Leopardi” until December 8, 2026
## Key facts - Place → MA*GA Museum of Gallarate - Central exhibition → «Jago. Bodies exposed" - Curator → Tommaso Zijno - Reorganization → «The museum of currents» - Third project → «Secondo Leopardi. From poetry to contemporary art" - Festival → Duemilalibri - Installation in Milan → «Water» - Tickets → TicketOne and MA*GA ticket office
### Three projects for the season On November 15, 2026, the MA*GA Museum in Gallarate opens a new exhibition season divided into three projects. The programming explores, through different approaches, the corporeal dimension, the social function of the museum institution and the link between literature and visual arts.
At the center is «Jago. Exposed bodies», exhibition curated by Tommaso Zijno and dedicated to the work of the sculptor Jago. The project puts his works in dialogue with those of Adolfo Wildt, Emilio Vedova, Salvatore Scarpitta and Marinella Pirelli. The exhibition will be accompanied by the rearrangement of the museum's collections through «The museum of currents», curated by Emma Zanella and Alessandro Castiglioni.
The third proposal is «According to Leopardi. From poetry to contemporary art", included in the program of Duemilalibri, the book and author festival of Gallarate. The exhibition brings back to MA*GA a nucleus of works linked to the relationship between the poetry of Giacomo Leopardi and the visual arts, with a contemporary reading of visual poetry.
The program therefore distributes the three initiatives between contemporary art, twentieth-century history and new interpretations of the museum's heritage. «Iago. Exposed bodies" and "The museum of currents" are scheduled from 15 November 2026 to 4 April 2027, while "Secondo Leopardi" is scheduled from 15 November to 8 December 2026.
The proposal does not end in the spaces of Gallarate. The project dedicated to Jago also includes a second intervention in Milan, at Palazzo Lombardia, where the installation «Water» will be presented. The two exhibitions are autonomous, but build a journey between Milan and Gallarate around the artist's research.
Tickets can be purchased in advance on TicketOne and at the MA*GA ticket office. The museum thus presents a season built on three different readings, united by the desire to connect contemporary works, memory of the twentieth century and the heritage of the collection. ### The body as surface and conflict The project “Jago. Exposed Bodies” begins with a comparison between Jago’s practice and that of four artists belonging to different periods and artistic languages. Jago, born in 1987, is placed alongside Adolfo Wildt, Emilio Vedova, Salvatore Scarpitta and Marinella Pirelli to construct a dialogue spanning more than a century of artistic research.
The exhibition is organized around two themes. The first is stripping away, understood as a gesture capable of revealing what lies beneath the surface. The second concerns war, presented as an extreme situation in which the body becomes a battleground. The itinerary therefore uses the human figure to address questions related to matter, violence and collective responsibility.
The resonances among the works connect Jago’s practice to Vedova’s gestural energy, Scarpitta’s material approach and Pirelli’s reflections on the political body. The comparison with Wildt takes on particular significance: like Jago, the sculptor used marble to bring out fragility, spirituality and pain.
Tommaso Zijno’s curatorial approach thus presents a reading of the body not limited to its physical dimension. Through the works brought together at MA*GA, the body becomes a tool for reflecting on power, violence, mysticism and collective responsibility. The chronological distance between the artists does not eliminate the connections, but makes it possible to follow transformations and continuities in artistic research.
### A collection read through currents “The Museum of Currents” instead stems from work on the historical archive of the Civic Gallery of Modern Art of Gallarate and from an analysis of the museographic concepts formulated by Silvio Zanella, the museum’s founder, between 1972 and 2000. The project is part of the activities of the Italia 2050 Research Center, founded in 2023 by Museo MAGA and the Lombardy Region.
Zanella envisioned a museum capable of telling the story not only of the development of artistic languages, but also of humanity, society and civilization in every era through those languages. The new installation takes up and updates this vision, abandoning a linear reading of art history in favor of a journey made up of returns, ruptures, accelerations and transformations.
There will also be a focus on research investigating the links between art, nature and ecology. The collection will thus be presented as an interweaving of currents and transitions, reinterpreted through relationships that go beyond chronological order alone. ### Leopardi between words and images «According to Leopardi. From poetry to contemporary art» completes the MA*GA program with an exhibition scheduled from November 15 to December 8, 2026, as part of Duemilalibri, Gallarate's book and author festival.
The project begins with a body of works that became part of the MA*GA collection following «Pages and Pages. 1798 / 1998 tribute to Giacomo Leopardi». In 1998, Gino Gini conceived the exhibition to mark the bicentenary of the birth of the poet from Recanati. That body is now being presented again through a contemporary interpretation that brings together visual poetry and artistic practices.
Among the artists featured in the exhibition are Tomaso Binga, Mirella Bentivoglio and Lamberto Pignotti. The relationship with Leopardi is therefore explored not only through literature, but also through works that engage with the visual dimension of the word and the possibilities of the image. The exhibition connects the museum's holdings with a contemporary reinterpretation of the poet from Recanati.
### The itinerary between Gallarate and Milan The program dedicated to Jago also extends to Palazzo Lombardia. From November 11, 2026, to January 10, 2027, the Milan venue will host «Water», an installation that juxtaposes the solidity of matter with the flow of time.
The Milan project and the Gallarate exhibition remain independent, but are presented as parts of a shared itinerary centered on the artist's research. The link between the two venues adds a second stop dedicated to Jago to the MA*GA season, distinct from the comparison between his works and those of Wildt, Vedova, Scarpitta and Pirelli.
The dates make it possible to follow a varied program. On November 15, 2026, «Jago. Bodies on display», «The museum of currents» and «According to Leopardi» will open in Gallarate, while Palazzo Lombardia will already have opened the «Water» project on November 11, 2026. The exhibition dedicated to Leopardi will end on December 8, 2026; the other two MA*GA initiatives will continue until April 4, 2027, and the Milan installation until January 10, 2027.
For access to the exhibitions, tickets can be purchased in advance on TicketOne and at the MA*GA ticket office. The museum thus rounds out the season with a program spread across Gallarate and Milan, keeping the individual projects distinct while connecting them through the themes of the body, the collection, and the relationship between poetry and the visual arts.
*Source: [varesenews.it](https://www.varesenews.it/2026/10/tre-nuove-mostre-al-maga-da-jago-a-leopardi/2709940/)*

item.title: Gallarate: Uto Ughi returns to Teatro Condominio with Vivaldi and Bach
item.description: Uto Ughi returns to Gallarate on October 25, 2026 Concert at 18 at Teatro Condominio Program dedicated to Vivaldi and Bach With the Virtuosi del Lemene and two soloists
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Uto Ughi returns to Gallarate on 25 October 2026 - Concert at 6 pm at the Teatro Condominio - Programme dedicated to Vivaldi and Bach - With the Virtuosi del Lemene and two soloists ## Key facts - Protagonist → Uto Ughi - Date → Sunday 25 October 2026 - Time → 6 pm - Venue → Teatro Condominio Vittorio Gassman, Gallarate - Repertoire → Antonio Vivaldi and Johann Sebastian Bach - Ensemble → Virtuosi del Lemene - Soloists → Glauco Bertagnin and Walter Zampiron - Tickets → Ticketone ### The concert On Sunday 25 October 2026, at 6 pm, Uto Ughi will be the protagonist at the Teatro Condominio Vittorio Gassman in Gallarate, for an event dedicated to great classical music. The famous violinist will return to the city's stage one year after his previous concert. He will be accompanied by the Virtuosi del Lemene, together with soloists Glauco Bertagnin on violin and Walter Zampiron on flute. The presence of the two musicians will complement that of the ensemble in a concert conceived as a dialogue between soloists and orchestra. The programme will be dedicated to Antonio Vivaldi and Johann Sebastian Bach. The evening will bring together some of the most famous and evocative compositions of the Baroque repertoire, in a selection that will highlight elegance and virtuosity. Ughi's return brings one of Italy's best-known international performers back to Gallarate. The programme and the participation of the Virtuosi del Lemene will help to highlight the legacy of classical music, creating a high-profile event. The event therefore stems from the meeting between the famous violinist, the ensemble that will accompany him and the two soloists chosen for the evening. The stage of the Teatro Condominio will thus host a musical journey focused on Vivaldi and Bach, with the violin and flute included in the programme dedicated to the Baroque repertoire. ## The return after a year ### The promise kept For Gallarate, the concert marks the return of an artist already known to the city. During last year’s event, Uto Ughi had met the city’s audience at Teatro Condominio, leaving open the possibility of performing again. The promise is now fulfilled with the concert on October 25. Councillor for Culture and Educational Activities Claudia Mazzetti linked the new event to the positive relationship the violinist had built with the venue, the audience and the city. “His return, after last year’s concert, gives me great pleasure: he had greatly appreciated the theatre, the audience and the welcome from the city of Gallarate. I am pleased that he kept his promise.” In Mazzetti’s comments, the evening is presented as an event of the highest calibre. The councillor also identifies two aims associated with the event: to showcase Uto Ughi, considered one of the world’s greatest violinists, and to bring classical music, described as a heritage, back to the forefront. With this event, Teatro Condominio continues its cultural journey, after hosting initiatives in different genres in recent years. The venue has alternated between drama and music, with the aim of broadening its offering and also making room again for the great classical repertoire. The new evening with Ughi thus fits within this path already outlined by the source. The previous meeting with the audience and the welcome received by the violinist are the elements that accompanied his return to the stage in Gallarate, alongside the desire to devote space to classical music. ## The event in Gallarate ### Date, venue and tickets The next event is scheduled for Sunday, October 25, at 18, at the Teatro Condominio “Vittorio Gassman” in Gallarate, at the corner of via Sironi and via Verdi. Tickets can be purchased through Ticketone. The venue will host Uto Ughi together with the Virtuosi del Lemene. Also taking the stage will be Glauco Bertagnin on violin and Walter Zampiron on flute, according to the lineup planned for the concert. The formation has been presented as part of the program built around Baroque music. The audience will enjoy an evening dedicated to Antonio Vivaldi and Johann Sebastian Bach. The announced program explores some of the best-known and most fascinating works in the Baroque repertoire and connects the presence of the soloists with that of the ensemble. The structure of the concert was conceived as a dialogue between soloists and orchestra. The roles indicated for the evening are therefore distinct: Uto Ughi will be the featured violinist, Glauco Bertagnin will join the program, also on violin, Walter Zampiron will perform on flute, and the Virtuosi del Lemene will accompany the renowned violinist. The October 25 event will thus bring together at the same venue the program dedicated to Vivaldi and Bach, the announced musicians, and Ughi’s return after last year’s concert. For the evening, the source confirms the time, the address of the Teatro Condominio and the availability of tickets on Ticketone. *Source: [varesenews.it](https://www.varesenews.it/2026/10/uto-ughi-torna-a-gallarate-al-teatro-condominio-una-serata-con-vivaldi-e-bach/2710177/)*

## TL;DR - Saturday 17 October: performance at the Teatro Regina Pacis in Saronno - Two replies scheduled at 3 p.m. and 4.30 p.m. - Representation of puppets with interaction with the public - Free souvenir photo provided with Bingo character
## Key facts Event: The new adventures of Masha and Bear Date: Saturday 17 October Place: Teatro Regina Pacis di Saronno Opening hours: 15:00 and 16:30 Company: The Fantastic Puppet World Contact: 392 8744754
Saturday, October 17, the Regina Pacis Theatre in Saronno will host the event entitled "The new adventures of Masha and the Bear". The show is offered by the company Il Fantastico Mondo dei Puppini and is mainly aimed at children, offering them the opportunity to meet live the protagonists of the stories they prefer. The organisation has planned two separate replicas to manage the flow of the public, setting appointments at 3 pm and 4.30 pm. This choice allows you to give different groups of children the opportunity to participate in the event at different times during the Saturday afternoon. The performance is part of a project that aims to combine pure entertainment with the tradition of figure theatre, an art that continues to fascinate new generations through the use of puppets and puppets handled by expert craftsmen of the scene. The event promises to be a moment of aggregation for families in the Saronno area and neighbouring municipalities, bringing the famous characters of the animated series to a physical and tangible dimension on the stage of the local theatre. ### Interaction and experience for children
The distinctive feature of this staging lies in the interactive nature of the show. Unlike classical theatrical performances where the audience remains passive, here there is the possibility for all the children present to interact verbally with the puppets during the development of the plot. This dynamic transforms the viewer into an active participant, allowing children to influence or comment on the adventures that are staged in real time. This pedagogical and playful approach serves to stimulate children's creativity and ability to express themselves orally, making the experience much more engaging than watching a cartoon on a screen.
In addition to the narrative aspect, the event includes a special moment dedicated to the memory of the experience. In fact, there is a free souvenir photo with Bingo for all young spectators. This detail adds an emotional value to the appointment, allowing the children to bring home a tangible memory of the encounter with the characters. The combination of the tradition of figure theatre and the use of modern and famous characters creates a bridge between different eras of children's entertainment, making the show an accessible and fun cultural product for the whole family, while enhancing the theatrical space as a place of discovery and play for children. ### Useful information and booking contacts
For those wishing to attend the performances on Saturday, October 17th at the Teatro Regina Pacis, the organization has provided a direct communication channel to obtain further information or clarification on the event details. The managers can be contacted via telephone at 392 8744754. To facilitate communication with parents and guardians, who often prefer quick and asynchronous messages, the number is also enabled for sending messages via the WhatsApp application. This tool allows for requests regarding potential costs, seat availability, or specific logistical details concerning theater entry.
The Saronno appointment represents an opportunity to rediscover figure theater in a modern context. The scheduling with two distinct times, 3:00 PM and 4:30 PM, suggests a desire for broad accessibility, seeking to avoid overcrowding and ensuring that every child can fully enjoy the interaction with the puppets. The choice of Teatro Regina Pacis as the venue emphasizes the importance of keeping the city's cultural centers alive, offering specific content for children that can attract families to the heart of the urban center. Interested parties are therefore invited to use the provided contacts to organize their visit and secure a spot for one of the two performances scheduled for Saturday, thus completing their weekend agenda dedicated to leisure and local culture.

item.title: Furia Award 2026 for Giovannini: sustainability at the center
item.description: 2026 Furia Award to Enrico Giovannini Economist and statistician, professor at Roma Tor Vergata He was Chief Statistician of the OECD and president of ISTAT ASviS founded
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Furia Award 2026 to Enrico Giovannini - Economist and statistician, lecturer at Roma Tor Vergata - He was Chief Statistician of the OECD and president of ISTAT - ASviS founded in 2016
## Key facts - Award → Premio Ecologia Città di Varese – Salvatore Furia 2026 - Recipient → Enrico Giovannini - Profile → economist and statistician - Positions → two-time minister, Chief Statistician of the OECD, president of ISTAT - Teaching → University of Rome Tor Vergata and National School of Administration - Agenda → United Nations 2030 Agenda - ASviS → founded in 2016 - Origin → Award founded by Salvatore Furia in 1973
The Premio Ecologia Città di Varese – Salvatore Furia 2026 is being awarded this year to Enrico Giovannini. The committee's decision concerns a figure who has transformed awareness of the environmental crisis into a reflection on the responsibilities of society, institutions and the economic system.
Giovannini is an economist and statistician. At the University of Rome Tor Vergata, he teaches Economic Statistics and Analysis and Policies for Sustainable Development as a full professor, in addition to teaching at the National School of Administration. Over the course of his career, he has been a two-time minister, Chief Statistician of the OECD and president of ISTAT.
He is co-founder and scientific director of the Italian Alliance for Sustainable Development, ASviS. The founding of the Alliance in 2016 represents a key milestone in a commitment to promoting the United Nations 2030 Agenda and a vision of development capable of bringing together the environmental, economic and social dimensions.
### The committee's rationale
The choice recognizes the scientific, institutional and public-outreach work through which Giovannini has placed sustainable development at the center of public debate. Well-being, in the perspective highlighted by the committee, does not coincide with economic growth alone: it includes quality of life, social cohesion, the protection of natural resources and the opportunities left to future generations.
### Salvatore Furia's legacy
The award thus recalls the figure of its founder, the naturalist and science communicator Salvatore Furia, who in 1973 linked knowledge of nature with education and the growth of the community. According to Nicoletta San Martino, councillor of the Municipality of Varese with responsibility for Environmental Protection, Social Sustainability and the Circular Economy, Furia's teaching instilled in young people a tangible sense of responsibility toward their local area:
> “To many young people, in addition to knowledge of nature, Furia passed on the ability to observe nature, learn about their own area and feel responsible for protecting it.”
The 2026 rationale therefore fits into his idea of environmental culture: understanding natural balances, recognizing human responsibility and turning awareness into responsible behavior. The choice links the recipient's profile to the tradition of the award: from knowledge of nature to collective responsibility, without separating the environment, society and the economy. The committee considers this transition consistent with Furia's cultural legacy. ## Sustainability as a lens
For the cross-border reader, the scope of the news is clear-cut. The source does not mention the G permit, AVS, LPP, LAMal, tax rebates, withholding tax or double taxation. It therefore provides no deadlines, amounts or procedures for those who work across the border: its subject is a cultural recognition and the way collective well-being is defined.
### From growth to well-being
What makes Giovannini’s choice broad in scope is moving beyond the separation between environmental and social policies. Sustainability is not described solely as the protection of natural resources. It also requires understanding how opportunities are distributed, who bears the costs of transformations and whether people can live in dignified conditions.
| Dimension | Framing indicated by the source | | Development | Not just economic growth, but quality of life and social cohesion | | Environment | Protection of ecosystems and natural resources | | Society | Combating poverty and inequalities, with inclusive and resilient communities | | Future | Opportunities for future generations and shared responsibilities |
This approach is the core of the integral ecology referred to in the recognition. The environmental crisis and the social crisis are not treated as separate problems: the former concerns natural balances, the latter the dignity of people and the conditions of the most vulnerable communities. Sustainability, therefore, requires a vision capable of connecting economic choices, institutions, social behavior and the protection of nature.
ASviS translates this perspective into the dissemination of the 2030 Agenda and its 17 Goals. The program combines the fight against poverty, the reduction of inequalities, the protection of ecosystems, the adoption of responsible practices in production and consumption, and the development of more inclusive and resilient societies. It is not a catalogue of separate topics: the source stresses their interdependence.
For those reading from a border region, the value of the news therefore lies in the lens it offers, not in a change to working life. The award invites us to ask whether a public decision considers the environment, economy and society together, and whether it distributes opportunities and costs fairly. These are the questions that connect Giovannini’s work to the institutional responsibility highlighted by the committee. ## Four steps for reading the award
The source makes it possible to follow a simple sequence to understand why the 2026 award is presented as the culmination of a cultural journey. There is no need to add tax or employment data: the content revolves around the connections between knowledge, culture, health, the economy and institutions.
### 1. Follow the path of the awards
The first step is to observe the series of the last five years through the recognitions mentioned. In 2022, Barbara Gallavotti represented the role of science communication in making complex knowledge accessible. In 2023, Michelangelo Pistoletto brought the relationship between culture, creativity, society and the planet into the award. In 2025, Ilaria Capua, with the vision of Salute Circolare, connected human health, animal health and environmental health, together with the impact of social behavior, the economy, law and information.
### 2. Identify the next step
The second step consists of reading Giovannini as the institutional and economic culmination of the sequence. After scientific knowledge, culture and health, the recognition focuses on how states regulate collective life, distribute opportunities and plan for the future. This is why the profile of an economist and statistician is included in an award dedicated to ecology.
### 3. Use the 17 Goals as a map
The third step is to verify the presence of the dimensions indicated by Agenda 2030: poverty and inequalities, ecosystems, responsible production and consumption, inclusive and resilient societies. The map serves to avoid reducing ecology to the mere conservation of nature and to recognize that environmental policies have social consequences.
### 4. Bring knowledge back to the community
The final step returns to Salvatore Furia’s method. Knowledge of natural balances must become awareness, and awareness must translate into responsible behavior. This is why education is part of sustainability: it does not remain specialized knowledge, but becomes a common heritage and involves society.
Read in this sequence, the news offers the public of Varese and readers beyond the borders a criterion for following the environmental debate without separating it from social and economic issues. The 2026 Premio Furia is not presented solely as an individual recognition, but as a stage in a culture of care.
*Source: [varesenews.it](https://www.varesenews.it/2026/10/il-premio-furia-sara-assegnato-alleconomista-enrico-giovannini/2708839/)*

item.description: Erreci Busto Arsizio beats Roma 3-1.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Erreci Busto Arsizio defeats Roma 3-1. - Three wins worth three points in women's A2. - Šiftar finishes with 24 points and 61% in attack. - Next challenge: Costa Volpino, Sunday, October 18.
## Key facts - Result → Erreci Busto Arsizio-Ferraro Smi Rome 3-1. - Partials → 22-25, 25-22, 25-22, 25-14. - Rank → 9 points and full score. - MVP → Emma Cagnin. - Next opponent → Costa Volpino at the Soevis Arena.
### The comeback after the first set
Erreci Busto Arsizio turned the midweek round into another leg of his clean sweep: Marchiaro's team beat Ferraro Smi Roma 3-1, after losing the first set, and remains full-scoring in the women's A2 championship.
For Futura Volley Giovani it is the third league game and the third three-point victory. After Perugia and Marsala, Rome also goes to the carpet: the whites climb to 9 and remain paired at Costa Volpino, waiting for the Altafratte match. The next opponent will be Costa Volpino at the Soevis Arena, on Sunday 18 October.
The Ferraro Smi starts better and wins the first set for 22-25, with Perovic in evidence; Edinara, returned from the injury, still offers a good contribution by scoring 5 points. Busto reacts in the second partial, won 25-22, with the Brazilian protagonist of the attacks from place 2. The finale also features Marconato, who was instrumental in repelling the last attempt at a Roman comeback.
The 25-22 is repeated in the third set. Šiftar grows with the passing of exchanges, while Cosi becomes impassable on the wall. Rome, having failed to return to the game, loses consistency and leaves the Futura free field in the fourth quarter, closed 25-14 with another dominant test of the Slovenian crusher.
Marchiaro explained that the team expected an aggressive Roma, but had started the contracted race, almost as if Busto had to lead the game. item.title: Gallarate: Azalee Calcio leave the field on Via Pradisera
item.description: Le Azalee Calcio leave the field on Via Pradisera.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Le Azalee Calcio leave the field on Via Pradisera. - The tender for the area received no bids. - Ugo Tomaselli denounces a substantial exclusion. - The Municipality points to the expired concession.
## Key facts - Location → field on Via Pradisera, Gallarate - Club → Azalee Calcio - President → Ugo Tomaselli - Tender → no bids - Athletics cage → nearly 25mila euro
Azalee Calcio announced on social media the return of the keys to the field on Via Pradisera, in Gallarate, after decades at the facility. The matter revolves around the tender for the concession of the area, which received no bids, but the two sides interpret it differently: the club speaks of being effectively ousted; the Municipality instead points to the expiry of the concession and the lack of conditions for a simple extension.
In the post published on social media, the club called the procedure improper and recalled its role in promoting women’s football, claiming to have made Gallarate known throughout Italy since 1980.
> “After fifty years, we’re out,” sums up president Ugo Tomaselli.
The president explained that he had waited for the new tender while assessing the work needed to continue operations at the facility. The possibilities considered included replacing the floodlights with LED fixtures and resurfacing the grass pitch.
### The tender and the required conditions
According to Tomaselli, the lack of participation was also due to the obligations imposed on the future concessionaire. Among the required works was a cage for athletics throwing events, whose cost the club estimated at nearly 25mila euro.
Until then, Atletica Gallaratese had used the spaces, paying Azalee sublease rent. Under the new arrangement, the structure would have had to be built. The president says that Atletica was unwilling to contribute and that Azalee could not bear the cost alone. The tender therefore received no bids.
After the bidding closed, the Municipality sent the club a Pec requesting the return of the facility. Tomaselli explained that neither requests for an extension nor the possibility of talks between the clubs had been enough to avoid the handover. The return of the keys therefore marks Azalee’s departure from the field on Via Pradisera, but leaves unresolved the dispute over management of the concession and the significance of the tender that received no bids. The Municipality's reconstruction starts from the facility's corporate history and does not coincide with that of Azalee. Mayor Andrea Cassani, who initially intervened by commenting on the post published by the company, distinguishes between the previous company awarded the concession and Azalee 1980, chaired by Ugo Tomaselli.
According to Cassani, the entity that today claims continuity with the Gallarate team would have a new corporate name and a new tax code. The transfer between the two companies, the mayor maintains, would never have been formally communicated to the Municipality. Azalee 1980 would have continued to play on the field on the basis of an agreement with the old company, but without an official communication to the administration.
Cassani also points to the financial situation of the previous management. According to what the mayor told VareseNews, the first company awarded the concession would have a debt crystallized as of 2023 amounting to 23,000 euros. The administration includes this figure in its own account of the dealings related to the facility.
The decisive point, however, remains the tender published to award the area. The mayor maintains that neither the old Azalee nor the new company took part in it. On the basis of this circumstance, he rejects the idea that the Municipality drove the team out: in the administration's view, the concessions had expired and no one had submitted a proposal to obtain the area again.
As for the extension, Cassani denies that it can be granted. Sports Councillor Claudia Mazzetti, by contrast, defends the Municipality's actions: she maintains that alternatives had been offered and that the situation had been explained clearly.
For the administration, the issue of the cage for athletics throwing events also remains open. Le Azalee had listed it among the obstacles to participating, since the project would have entailed an investment intended for another discipline. Cassani attributes the decision not to build it to the company and hypothesizes that, if the area is assigned again, the work could be the responsibility of another party.
The positions therefore remain far apart over the origin of the split. The company considers the request to hand back the area the outcome of an improper procedure; the Municipality links it to the expiry of the concession, the tender with no bids, and the absence of the conditions for an extension. The rest of the story mainly concerns the continuity of the Azalee's sporting activities after leaving the field on via Pradisera. The club had two women's teams and a men's team. After the keys were handed back, president Tomaselli explained that only the men's team will play at Majno. As for training, however, a solution still needs to be found.
The consequence described by the club therefore concerns not only the availability of the facility, but also the possibility of keeping the various teams organized. The men's team has an indicated destination, while no arrangement has been found for training activities. The Azalee also lament the loss of the teams, directly linking the abandonment of the field to the difficulty of continuing the sporting project.
### The closed field and the future of the area
Meanwhile, the historic football field remains padlocked. The return requested by the Municipality thus had an immediate effect on access to the facility, without the discussions between the clubs leading to the extension requested by the Azalee or to the opening of the meeting proposed by the president.
From an administrative standpoint, the Municipality confirms that the concession cannot be extended. The future of the area is thus tied to a new award, mentioned by Cassani as the possibility through which another party could build the cage needed for athletics throwing events. The work therefore remains associated with the subsequent management of the facility and not with the continuation of the Azalee's activities.
The situation leaves two distinct aspects open. On the one hand, there is the management of the area, which received no offers in the tender and has the field closed. On the other hand, there is sporting continuity, which for the Azalee means moving the men's team to Majno and seeking spaces for training. The source does not describe a new concessionaire or an already defined solution for the women's teams. The firm point, instead, is the one indicated by the Municipality: no extension for the expired concession and the prospect that any new concessionaire could take care of the athletics facility.

item.title: OCST history: from 1919 to protecting cross-border commuters in Ticino
item.description: The Chamber of Labor was founded in 1902.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The Chamber of Labour was established in 1902. - OCST was founded on May 18, 1919. - The statutes were adopted on November 16 in Bellinzona. - Many cross-border workers unionized during the boom.
## Key facts - Origin → workers' societies founded on solidarity and mutual aid - Economic turning point → Gotthard Railway, 1882 - Chamber of Labour → 1902 - OCST → May 18, 1919 - Statutes → November 16, 1919, Bellinzona - Magazine → Il Lavoro, since 1920 - Secretary → don Luigi Del Pietro, since September 1, 1929 - Cross-border workers → many were unionized during the economic boom
### From solidarity to founding Around the middle of the nineteenth century, in a poor Canton Ticino where agriculture and pastoralism were the main activities, the first small workers' societies based on solidarity and mutual aid were established. The construction of the Gotthard Railway in 1882 changed the canton's economy: agriculture began to decline, while factories, tourism and services appeared in the towns. According to the account presented in January 2021, this turning point was the result of a long social transformation.
The workers' association movement was promoted by Italian immigrants and Ticinese emigrants, who had encountered more advanced social conditions abroad. At the end of the nineteenth century, the first socialist trade unions were established. In 1902, the Chamber of Labour and, in Catholic circles, the Cantonal Circle for Political and Social Studies were formed.
The appeal of Rerum Novarum by Leone XIII, in 1891, had initially left the Catholic world of Ticino indifferent. Thanks to the initiative of don Carlo Roggero, the first Catholic Workers' Leagues spread, particularly in the Locarnese and Bellinzonese areas. In Locarno, in 1906, a permanent secretariat was established; the Bollettino del Bureau Popolare became La Gazzetta del Lavoratore the following year.
The First World War worsened workers' conditions throughout Switzerland. In November 1918, there was a three-day general strike in the main Swiss centers. A group of Christian-social workers was formed in Bellinzona. In 1919, the Federation of Christian-Social Trade Unions was founded; on May 18, OCST was officially established in Ticino. The statutes were adopted on November 16 in Bellinzona. Il Lavoro began in 1920 and ceased in 1927.
Don Luigi Del Pietro became secretary on September 1, 1929, after the bishop of Lugano, Mons. Aurelio Bacciarini, decided to entrust the union to him. Inspired by the social teaching of the Church, he relaunched OCST despite the hostility of socialist trade unions, part of the employers and respectable society. In 1933, he resumed Il Lavoro and opened the Casa del Popola in Lugano. By the end of the 1930s, OCST had matched the Chamber of Labour in membership and later became the most representative trade union in Ticino. Del Pietro's death in 1977 led to internal restructuring. ## The link with cross-border work ### What emerges for the cross-border worker The link with cross-border work appears in a specific passage: during the years of the economic boom, OCST was at the forefront of protecting foreign workers and significantly increased its membership, also thanks to the unionization of many cross-border workers. For a cross-border worker, this is the key point to retain: their presence becomes part of the history of the union within the growth of employment in Ticino and the services that OCST consolidated.
The economic context described by the source helps put that passage in perspective without separating it from the rest of the labor market. In the 1950s and until the beginning of the 1970s, construction, tourism and services expanded, while major hydroelectric projects and new roads accompanied the Canton of Ticino's entry into modernity. People from Ticino entered mainly the tertiary sector, while immigrants entered the secondary sector. With the abundance of jobs, union activity lost some of its vitality, but contributed to building the welfare state.
| Passage | What emerges from the source | |---|---| | Economic boom | Expansion of construction, tourism, services and hydroelectric works | | Collective protection | Widespread collective agreements in many professions | | Crisis 1973-76 | Increase in unemployment, largely exported to foreign workers | | 1980s | Potential for a new cross-border reality, together with new pockets of poverty |
This sequence makes it possible to distinguish the collective dimension from the individual one. The source discusses the protection of foreign workers, collective agreements, services and regional offices; it does not describe an individual dispute, a payslip or a procedure for obtaining a benefit. Therefore, the cross-border worker can understand the historical role of union representation, but not get a personal answer about a contractual situation.
The text contains no information about G permit, AVS, LPP, LAMal, withholding tax, tax rebates or double taxation. There are no references to INPS, the Brogeda border crossing or any possible new 2026 tax agreement. For these matters, the page is not the appropriate source; its contribution remains a reconstruction of the time when the union engaged with foreign and cross-border workers. ## How to read the history operationally ### Four steps for orientation To use the reconstruction correctly, it is advisable to follow a simple procedure: read the steps in order, distinguish the forms of organization, and stick to the data actually provided. The source recounts the historical evolution of OCST and work in Ticino; it does not provide an individual procedure for cross-border workers.
1. Start with the economy. Situate workers' societies in the agricultural Ticino of the mid-nineteenth century and use 1882, the year of the Gotthard railway, as a turning point toward factories, tourism and services.
2. Distinguish the actors. Separate the associations promoted by Italian immigrants and emigrated Ticinese, the socialist trade unions, the Catholic Workers' Leagues and OCST.
3. Follow representation. Relate collective agreements, protection for foreign workers, services and regional offices to the unionization of many cross-border workers during the boom.
4. Respect the scope. Do not turn the reconstruction into an answer about an individual employment relationship: the text provides no amounts, forms or administrative instructions.
Places also help verify the sequence. The Locarnese and Bellinzonese indicate the area of the first Catholic Workers' Leagues; Locarno hosted the permanent secretariat; Bellinzona was the site of the first Christian-social group and the adoption of the statutes. Lugano enters the trajectory with Casa del Popola and the headquarters at via Balestra 19, inaugurated in 1971.
The dates in the source are historical references, not operational deadlines. The reader can use them to distinguish the emergence of associations, the foundation of OCST, the relaunch phase under Del Pietro and the subsequent restructuring. For a cross-border worker, the most concrete point remains the one indicated by the source: during the economic boom, many workers from across the border became unionized through OCST. item.title: Generic drugs: how much more does Switzerland pay
item.description: Ten generic drugs: 241,56 francs in Switzerland.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Ten generics: 241,56 francs in Switzerland. - One month costs 2,9 times the average of the three neighboring countries. - Metformin: 10,85 francs in Ticino versus 1,39 in Austria. - ECB exchange rate: 1 euro = 0,9359 francs on October 6, 2026.
## Key facts Sample → ten generic drugs for everyday use. Quantity → 30 tablets for one month of treatment. Switzerland → 241,56 francs. Germany → 118 francs. Italy → 76 francs. Austria → 55 francs. Difference → from 1.8 times for candesartan to 4.6 times for metformin. Exchange rate → 1 euro = 0,9359 francs, according to the ECB exchange rate of October 6, 2026.
Ten active ingredients, four markets and a simple criterion: thirty tablets for each monthly treatment. The comparison places Switzerland, Germany, Italy and Austria side by side, using the cheapest generic available for ten everyday medicines. These are products used to treat cholesterol, high blood pressure, heartburn, diabetes, depression or to prevent heart attacks and strokes.
Same active ingredient, same dosage and, often, the same manufacturer. The selection uses the cheapest generic on the market and the retail list price, including VAT. The Swiss basket comes to 241,56 francs; the German one to 118 francs, the Italian one to 76 and the Austrian one to 55.
### The cases that shift the total
Metformin is the clearest case. For the cheapest generic, a pharmacy in Ticino charges 10,85 francs for a pack of 30 tablets. In Austria, the health insurance fund pays the equivalent of 1,39 francs, including VAT, an amount eight times lower. In Italy, by contrast, the equivalent pack costs 2,23 euros.
Atorvastatin also maintains a wide gap. The cheapest generic costs 30,25 francs in Switzerland; in Como, the equivalent pack costs 7,96 euros, approximately 7,45 francs. In Germany the price is 13,33 euros, while in Austria the health insurance fund reimburses 5,10 euros plus VAT.
The comparison also produces a paradox: the Swiss generic may cost more than the original sold across the border. Sanofi’s original Plavix costs 17,07 euros in Italy, approximately 16 francs; the cheapest generic clopidogrel in Switzerland comes to 34,70 francs, more than double. In the Swiss sample, the generic costs on average, according to the median, 18% less than the branded product, but for clopidogrel the difference is almost nil and for metformin it is 20 cents.
For a cross-border commuter looking at the relationship between Italy and Canton Ticino, this is a snapshot of drug prices, not a measure of a G permit, AVS, LPP or LAMal. The text compares packs, VAT and reimbursements, not administrative rules. ## Why the gap widens
The gap cannot be explained solely by the molecule. The analysis attributes it mainly to distribution margins and pricing rules that are not very competitive. To read the result correctly, however, it is necessary to separate the retail price from the ex-factory price and distinguish the list price from the amount actually reimbursed.
### List price, reimbursement and international comparison
| Comparison | Reported result | |---|---| | Swiss sample | The generic costs, at the median, 18% less than the original. | | Meierhans, November 2024 | The cheapest foreign generic accounts for an average of 39% of the Swiss price; in the United Kingdom the percentage is 16%. | | santésuisse and Interpharma, end of May 2024 | Abroad, generics are 45,3% cheaper; for biosimilars the gap is 29,9%, while for patent-protected drugs it falls to 8,9%. |
Stefan Meierhans's comparison with 15 European countries leads to the conclusion that, on average, Swiss generics cost more than twice as much. The annual analysis by santésuisse and Interpharma reaches a similar result, but uses ex-factory prices: it does not include distribution margins and taxes. The basket examined, on the other hand, uses the retail price, the one that appears on the health insurer's or patient's bill. It is this basic difference that explains why the gap may appear larger.
The Swiss basket exceeds the German one by 105%, the Italian one by 218% and the Austrian one by 336%. Even excluding VAT, which is 19% in Germany and 2,6% in Switzerland, the ratio compared with Germany remains 2,4 to 1.
Germany shows the other side of the problem. The list price of the original is much higher: 30 tablets of Crestor cost 92,81 euros, compared with 13,42 euros for generic rosuvastatin. Health insurers, however, reimburse only up to the Festbetrag; anyone who wants the branded product pays the difference. In Austria, Sortis and Plavix are not listed in the Reimbursement Code: insurers reimburse only generics.
For a cross-border commuter, the practical takeaway is not to treat a Swiss retail price, a German list price and an Austrian reimbursement as equivalent. They are three different figures, even when they concern the same therapy. ## How to redo the comparison
The comparison method can become a small checking procedure for anyone who needs to compare a price in francs with one in euros. The rule is to keep the product, quantity, taxes, and price basis constant. Without these steps, the comparison risks mixing a generic with an original or a reimbursement with a list price.
### Five steps
1. Start with the active ingredient and dosage. The original's commercial name may change from one country to another; for this reason, the reference is the substance indicated in the therapy. The comparison points out that, often, the manufacturer is also the same.
2. Set the quantity at 30 tablets. This is the unit used to represent one month of therapy and allows equivalent packages to be compared, rather than stopping at the price of a box with a different number of doses.
3. Choose the least expensive generic available in each country. The comparison cart selects, for each of the ten active ingredients, the least costly option on the market.
4. Write down the retail price and VAT. The main figure is the one that ends up on the invoice of the health insurer or patient. For Austria, it should be noted when the reference is the amount paid by the health insurer; for Germany, the list price must be distinguished from the amount covered up to the Festbetrag.
5. Bring all amounts into the same currency. The ECB exchange rate indicated by the comparison is that of October 6, 2026: 1 euro = 0.9359 francs. Only after conversion can the totals and differences between the four countries be compared.
If one also wants to verify the ratio between originals and generics, the same discipline must be maintained. The comparison considers eight originals available in all four countries: the total is 226 francs in Switzerland, 56 in Austria, 69 in Italy, and 419 in Germany. The latter figure, however, is a list price that German health insurers do not reimburse beyond the generic's fixed amount.
For a cross-border commuter comparing a therapy between Italy and Switzerland, the useful difference is therefore not merely the final number: it is important to know whether one is looking at a generic, an original, a retail price, or a reimbursement. The comparison remains readable for each individual drug as well, from the 1.8-times ratio for candesartan to 4.6 times for metformin.
To quickly redo the conversion between euros and francs, use the comparatore CHF/EUR.

item.title: Border resignations: deadlines and procedure
item.description: How to resign in Ticino: terms of notice, impact on G leave and unemployment.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The Swiss notice period ranges from 1 to 3 months - The resignation must be in writing and delivered to the employer - The impact on the G permit and unemployment rights is critical ## Key facts - **Minimum notice period**: 1 month - Maximum notice period: 3 months (after 10 years of service) - Format: Written (registered mail recommended) - Involved entities: SECO, USTAT, INPS The decision to leave a job in Ticino as a cross-border worker is not just a professional choice, but a legal act with concrete repercussions on taxation and social security. In Switzerland, the Code of Obligations establishes the notice periods, which start at one month for the first two years of service, rising to two months after two years and to three months after ten years of seniority with the same employer. These terms are not strictly negotiable, but they can be modified by the individual contract only in a manner more favorable to the worker, never to their detriment. ### The resignation procedure The resignation must be communicated in writing. Although the law does not mandate registered mail, it is the only certain proof of receipt. The employer is obliged to issue a work certificate (LAVS) at the end of the employment relationship, a document essential for any future employment in Switzerland. Without this certificate, the professional career in the Canton of Ticino is significantly affected. It is fundamental to verify that the certificate contains the exact end date of the relationship, the qualification performed and, if requested, the main activity. A cross-border worker who finds themselves in a situation of voluntary resignation must be aware that this choice will also influence their rights in terms of social security and taxation, particularly regarding the management of the G permit and potential registration for unemployment. ### Impact on G permit and taxation The termination of the employment relationship directly affects the validity of the G permit. If the cross-border worker does not find new employment in Ticino within a reasonable time frame, the permit may be revoked. Furthermore, voluntary resignation results in a waiting period for unemployment benefits. In Switzerland, anyone who voluntarily resigns without a valid reason recognized by law (such as unfair dismissal or a substantial modification of contractual terms) is subject to a waiting period for unemployment benefits. The duration of this waiting period varies, but it prevents immediate access to benefits managed by the SECO (State Secretariat for Economic Affairs) or the competent cantonal funds. On the tax side, withholding tax is deducted directly by the employer. In the event of resignation, it is important to verify that the withholding is correct for the period worked. Italian cross-border workers benefit from a tax credit in Italy to avoid double taxation, regulated by the Italo-Swiss Convention of March 9, 1976. The CE section of the Italian 730 tax return is the tool for declaring income from work in Switzerland. A cross-border worker who resigns must ensure that the employment certificate and tax statements are consistent in order to correctly complete the tax return. INPS and the Italian Revenue Agency (Agenzia delle Entrate) are the reference bodies for managing social security and taxation in Italy, while in Switzerland the relevant institutions are the SECO for unemployment and the USTAT for industry statutes and regulations. ### Operational checklist for resignations Before sending the cancellation letter, it is advisable to follow a structured procedure to minimize bureaucratic risks. First, check the exact contractual and legal notice period. Secondly, write the letter clearly and concisely, indicating the last date of work. Deliver the letter by registered mail with return receipt or, if possible, in person with signature of receipt. Keep a copy and proof of delivery. After the end of the relationship, immediately request the work certificate. Check that the data is correct. If you are entitled to a holiday allowance, make sure it is paid or compensated. As far as social security is concerned, AVS (Old Age and Survivors Insurance) and AI (Disability Insurance) continue to be registered, no matter where you live. If you decide to look for a job in Ticino, register with the competent employment office. On the other hand, if you return to Italy, check how the contributions paid in Switzerland affect your right to a pension through bilateral agreements. To calculate the net impact of your resignation and estimate the taxes due, you can use our simulation tool. The calculator helps you understand how withholding tax translates into your net salary and how to manage the tax credit in Italy. Simula il tuo stipendio netto

item.description: The Presidio Vivo project gets underway in Olgiate Olona Two squares host the participating markets Easily identifiable volunteers assist the Local Police Events
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The Presidio Vivo project gets underway in Olgiate Olona - Two squares host the markets involved - Clearly identifiable volunteers work alongside the Local Police - Events scheduled through December
## Key facts - Project → Presidio Vivo - Locations → piazza Don Pino Ballabio and piazza Volontari della Libertà - Volunteers → Market Sentinels - Coordination → Local Police - Call for proposals → urban security - Scheduling → events through December
### A recognizable presence in the markets
Two squares in Olgiate Olona are at the center of Presidio Vivo, the new security initiative promoted by the municipal administration through participation in a regional call for proposals dedicated to urban security.
One of the project's objectives is to strengthen the monitoring and community-outreach activities already active in the area's main market areas. The markets involved are located in piazza Don Pino Ballabio, in the historic center, and in piazza Volontari della Libertà, in the Buon Gesù neighborhood.
These are places that the municipality considers important meeting points for residents, shopkeepers and visitors. The two squares host the town's markets and represent spaces where daily presence combines with commercial activities and with people visiting the town.
During market days, security is already ensured by the presence of the Olgiate Olona Local Police. The officers provide monitoring services, traffic management and support for citizens. Presidio Vivo is designed to further strengthen this work through complementary actions involving civic presence, information and awareness-raising.
The project therefore places a recognizable volunteer presence in market locations alongside the services already provided by the Local Police. Coordination remains entrusted to the Local Police, while the planned activities aim to make attention to public spaces and the needs of those who use them more visible.
Among the initiatives are the Market Sentinels: easily recognizable volunteers who will offer support in managing spaces, welcoming and guiding market-goers. Their work will always take place under the coordination of the Local Police.
The decision to involve volunteers and associations places the project in a community-oriented framework. The market is considered not only a place to shop, but also a space for interaction and presence, where welcome and guidance can complement the monitoring already provided by officers. ## Information and community policing
The information component of Presidio Vivo is also delivered through the Local Police's community help desk. The project provides for the opening of a dedicated point for citizens, where they can receive advice and information on topics related to security and the care of shared spaces.
### From scams to the care of public spaces
The Help Desk will focus on preventing scams targeting older people, road safety, respect for public spaces, and urban upkeep. These are different issues, but they are all linked to everyday life in market areas and to the possibility for citizens to engage directly with the Local Police.
The local presence will involve officers together with volunteer associations invited to participate in the initiative. Among them, the source names the Associazione Nazionale Carabinieri in Congedo di Castellanza and the Pro Loco di Olgiate Olona. The project thus aims to combine information, assistance, and collaboration with organizations already active in the community.
Presidio Vivo also stands alongside other measures adopted by the municipal administration in the area of urban security. The initiative includes the expansion of video surveillance, with a significant increase in the number of cameras operating across the area, and the strengthening of monitoring services.
The Municipality also highlights the joint work between the Local Police Commands of Olgiate Olona and Solbiate Olona. The agreement has led to an increase in joint patrols and surveillance services, giving monitoring activities an inter-municipal dimension.
Councillor for Commerce and Digitalization Fabio Longhin presented the new project as part of a strategy based on presence, prevention, and collaboration with the community.
> «Presidio Vivo adds a new element to a strategy based on presence, prevention, and collaboration with the community».
The initiatives mentioned by Longhin also include the recent Patti per la Legalità, signed with S.O.S. Italia Libera, an anti-racketeering and anti-usury association, as well as with students at the Dante Alighieri secondary school. The administration has also supported the development of Controllo del Vicinato networks, involving both citizens and the business community.
According to the approach outlined by the councillor, video surveillance, coordinated Local Police services, prevention initiatives, and neighborhood networks are different but complementary tools. The stated goal is to help build a more aware, attentive, and cohesive community, without separating monitoring from citizens' participation. ## Appointments through December
The project will be developed through a schedule of events spread over the months through December. The planned presence in the area will include Local Police officers and the volunteer organizations involved in the initiative, with activities concentrated in the spaces hosting the town markets.
### Markets as community spaces
The schedule will complement the ordinary presence of the Local Police with the activities of the Market Sentinels, welcoming market-goers and providing guidance in the areas concerned. These actions will be joined by the Neighborhood Help Desk, conceived as an information point for residents on prevention, road safety, respect for public spaces and urban decorum.
Mayor Giovanni Montano linked this phase to recognizing the role of associations and volunteers in the town’s most frequented places. The choice concerns the markets in particular, described as spaces for relationships, social interaction and everyday presence.
For the administration, increasing the safety of these places helps strengthen the sense of community and spread a shared culture of prevention. In the mayor’s view, safety depends not only on monitoring tools, but also on an attentive and engaged community.
The role assigned to shopkeepers, volunteers, associations, schools and residents is to collaborate in promoting awareness, civic-mindedness and care for shared spaces. The direction chosen by Olgiate Olona is described as community-based safety, founded on collaboration and shared responsibility.
The project’s operational follow-up is therefore linked to a visible and coordinated presence in the two market squares. On the one hand, there will be Local Police officers engaged in monitoring activities, traffic management and supporting residents; on the other, volunteers and associations will contribute to welcoming visitors, providing guidance and caring for the spaces.
The Municipality identifies the ultimate goal as strengthening the sense of safety and improving quality of life in public spaces. Presidio Vivo also intends to promote the town markets as places of social interaction, meeting and participation, through a visible, collaborative presence attentive to the needs of the community.

item.title: Como, don Giusto welcomes the Gloria shows at Teatro Nuovo
item.description: The Gloria Cinema is closed for fire-safety compliance Don Giusto offers the Teatro Nuovo di Rebbio Sunday the 18th at 16 the Barabàn-Musica Spiccia concert
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Cinema Gloria is closed for fire-safety compliance work - Father Giusto offers Teatro Nuovo di Rebbio - The Barabàn-Musica Spiccia concert on Sunday the 18th at 16:00 - The celebrated Cinema Mondays also continue
## Key facts - Space → Cinema Gloria, via Varesina - Operator → Circolo Arci Xanadù - Performance venue → Teatro Nuovo di Rebbio - Reason for closure → bringing the premises into compliance with fire-safety regulations - Reading → Palestinians are your eyes - Concert → Barabàn and Musica Spiccia, Sunday the 18th at 4 p.m. - Financial support → proceeds from the performances
### From via Varesina to Teatro Nuovo The sudden closure of the Cinema Gloria auditorium on via Varesina has moved Circolo Arci Xanadù's performances to Teatro Nuovo di Rebbio. The theater was made available by don Giusto Della Valle, parish priest of Rebbio, who accepted the request from the association responsible for managing the neighborhood's historic cinema.
The Gloria needs to be brought into compliance with fire-safety regulations and, in the meantime, the space has been closed. The parish's availability thus makes it possible to maintain the events listed in the original program, even if in a different venue from the usual one.
The evening's program includes the theatrical reading Palestinians are your eyes. The event on Sunday the 18th at 4 p.m. will instead be a folk concert featuring the Milan-based Barabàn and the Como-based Musica Spiccia. After these events, the celebrated Cinema Mondays will also continue.
The solution therefore concerns the activities already scheduled by Circolo Arci Xanadù. No new calendar is being announced, but rather the continuation of initiatives that had been organized for the Gloria and that now have a venue in the theater in Rebbio. The move makes it possible not to interrupt the events mentioned in the source during the closure of the auditorium on via Varesina.
Don Giusto's role is to provide a venue for the association's performances. His availability comes as the Gloria continues to deal with the work required to bring it into compliance with fire-safety regulations. The link between the closure and the new venue is therefore direct: on the one hand, the cinema space cannot host the activities; on the other, Teatro Nuovo is being made available so that the program can continue.
The story concerns a cultural and community organization in the Rebbio neighborhood, but also involves the city of Como, where the Gloria is a well-known venue for its activities. The announced events are the first practical follow-up to the closure: the reading, the folk concert and the continuation of Cinema Mondays are being transferred to the parish setting in Rebbio. ## Arci di Como's response
### Gianpaolo Rosso's message The availability of Teatro Nuovo was welcomed by Arci di Como. Gianpaolo Rosso, president of Arci di Como, expressed this in a statement entitled Thank you to Father Giusto Della Valle. The message presents the parish's intervention not merely as a solution for the performances, but as a sign of the relationship between the social entities present in the area.
Within the neighborhood and beyond its borders, Arci di Como sees the Parrocchia di Rebbio, Rebbio solidale, and Father Giusto Della Valle as the greatest hope for the future in times marked by selfishness, inequalities, environmental devastation, wars, and genocides.
Rosso highlights the physical proximity among the different organizations. On Via Lissi, just a few meters apart, are the parish and the headquarters of the provincial committee, together with many Arci clubs. A short distance away, on Varesina, however, is Spazio Gloria. In the statement, the president specifies that Gloria is not merely a cinema: Arci Xanadù makes it available as a common good.
This concentration of places and activities gives rise to the idea of an area capable of becoming a first example of a liberated city, without restrictive territorial boundaries. This interpretation broadens the meaning of the availability of Teatro Nuovo: support for the club is placed within a local network made up of a parish, associations, and spaces for social interaction.
The president of Arci di Como also links Father Giusto's choice to the social, political, cultural, and human development of the area. According to Rosso, this development is a shared activity and constitutes the foundation of the convergence policy also invoked by the parish priest. He adds that, if the municipality does not understand its value, Arci will act more forcefully.
In the section devoted to the closure, Rosso speaks of a very serious blow inflicted by the paper rituals of an oppressive bureaucracy. He distinguishes this matter from the issue of safety and states that safety at Gloria was, is, and will always be guaranteed. The availability of Teatro Nuovo is therefore described as generous, timely, and lifesaving for the club.
The statement concludes with a further thank-you addressed to Father Giusto, the parish, Rebbio solidale, and the many groups that find in the oratory spaces for social interaction and incubators of generative political activities. Rosso considers these places a common heritage, not property, and defines the theater's offer as the latest gesture of solidarity, or rather of sharing. ## The expenses and the Gloria mon amour campaign
### Sinistra Italiana's appeal The economic issue is explicit. The proceeds from the shows are essential for Circolo Arci Xanadù, because they make it possible to raise the resources needed to complete the code-compliance work on the Gloria and to ensure that those who work there are paid. The closure of the venue therefore also interrupts the income linked to the activities held in the hall.
On this point, Sinistra Italiana Como spoke out, expressing its closeness to Circolo Arci Xanadù over the closure of Spazio Gloria. The statement refers to adaptation works that had already been scheduled but not yet completed. The Gloria is described as a point of reference for associations in Como and, because of the richness and originality of its cultural offerings, as an important space for social interaction and the dissemination of culture for the neighborhood and the city of Como.
Sinistra Italiana's position concerns above all the decision to impose the closure when the final works were already planned. The statement says it is difficult to understand how, after adaptation works that had dragged on over time despite economic difficulties, such a serious measure was adopted precisely when the final works had already been scheduled.
The appeal is addressed to supporters and the public. Sinistra Italiana asks people to contribute, each according to their means, to covering the expenses that the association will have to face in the absence of revenue. The costs mentioned include salaries and rents, in addition to the expenses for completing the adaptation works.
The fundraising is linked to the Gloria mon amour campaign. The statement points out that several Sinistra Italiana activists have already contributed and also invites other supporters and citizens to take part. The message therefore does not separate the defense of the cultural space from the problem of the resources needed by the association.
The follow-up described by the source unfolds on two fronts. On the one hand, Teatro Nuovo's availability makes it possible to host the scheduled shows and keep the initiatives on the program active. On the other hand, Arci Xanadù must cover current expenses and those related to completing the Gloria's code-compliance work.
The reactions of Arci di Como and Sinistra Italiana Como converge on the local value of the space and the need to support its activities. The former emphasizes the solidarity of the parish and Rebbio solidale; the latter highlights the Gloria mon amour campaign and the expenses for salaries, rents and works. These are the developments indicated by the source after the closure of the hall on via Varesina.
*Source: [comozero.it](https://comozero.it/attualita/como-il-parroco-salva-larci-don-giusto-accoglie-al-teatro-nuovo-gli-spettacoli-del-cinema-gloria-chiuso-per-lanticendio/)*

item.title: Varese: the stadium forecourt is named after Anastasi
item.description: The Franco Ossola forecourt bears the name of Pietro Anastasi The plaque was installed by the Municipality The naming was approved unanimously In Masnago
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The Franco Ossola forecourt bears the name of Pietro Anastasi - The plaque was installed by the Municipality - The naming was approved unanimously - In Masnago, the tribute brought together teammates and supporters
## Key facts - Location → square in front of Franco Ossola Stadium - Honoree → Pietro Anastasi - Choice → dedication approved unanimously - Origin → Catania - Plaque → recalls Anastasi's rise as a champion in Varese and the memory Italy has preserved of him - Remembered figures → Ambrogio Borghi, Gedeone Carmignani and Roberto Bettega - National team → 1968 European Championship final in Rome
### The ceremony in Masnago
The square in front of Franco Ossola Stadium, in Masnago, now bears the name of Pietro Anastasi. The tribute took place in front of what had been his home as an athlete and celebrated one of the most representative figures in Varese sports and Varese Calcio. The dedication honors not only the champion but also the man, remembered as generous, humble and unforgettable.
The red-and-white roses were in Mrs. Anna's hands. Emotion could be heard in Gianluca's voice, while those who, over the course of his life and career, had known, loved and cheered for Pietro Anastasi gathered in the square. The moment brought together the memory of the goalscorer and that of the man appreciated by those who had come to Masnago for the occasion.
The decision to dedicate the area to him was described as right, deserved and appreciated, as well as approved unanimously. The Municipality installed the plaque bearing a dedication to Anastasi. The image depicts him in the red-and-white jersey as he looks toward the entrance to the Franco Ossola. The marker placed in front of the stadium thus makes the square's naming and its connection with the facility that was his home as an athlete visible.
Anastasi was born far away from here, in Catania. Yet it was precisely in Varese that he grew up, made his name and returned to live after appearing on the major stages of Italian and international football. His journey therefore connects his Catanian origins with the relationship he built with Varese, without separating his sporting career from the life he lived after returning.
For this reason, the name on the square brings together in one place the stadium, Varese Calcio and the memory of Pietro Anastasi. The ceremony gathered the affection of those who were present in person or in spirit and gave the recognition a dimension tied to the city as well as to sport. Anastasi's name is thus placed right in front of the stadium entrance, identified as the place of his experience as an athlete, within a ceremony designed to remember the champion and the man together. ## The memories of those who knew him
### A symbol for Varese
Ambrogio Borghi, who was Anastasi's teammate, summed up in the shortest and most incisive phrase of the day the meaning of the bond between the footballer and Varese.
> “If Naples has Maradona, Varese has Anastasi”
For Borghi, Anastasi's time with the red-and-white side was relatively brief, but it marked an era and linked him to the finest and strongest Varese team of all time. The phrase sums up the weight the player had in the city's sporting history, even beyond the length of his time wearing the red-and-white shirt.
Gedeone Carmignani focused above all on the striker's qualities. In his assessment, Anastasi knew how to move into space, had a nose for goal and was willing to press. With these qualities, he would be useful to every coach today. The assessment portrays a player capable of combining a presence in the box with a willingness to work even without the ball, as recalled during the meeting in Masnago.
The group of guests also used words tied to the personal dimension of the remembrance. Generous, always present and modest were the adjectives used to describe a man who was always there when someone sought him out. In this image, Pietro is not only the goalscorer celebrated in sporting memory, but a person to turn to and from whom to receive help. It is the human quality that accompanied the remembrance of his career.
Roberto Bettega came from Turin, linked to Anastasi by having played for Varese, Juventus and the national team. Bettega recalled the period when, upon returning to Juventus, the two were roommates. He scored immediately, then went scoreless for many matches; Anastasi stood by him, helped him, and his teammate began scoring again. The testimony brings a specific episode of personal support into the ceremony, distinct from the account of goals and jerseys worn.
The words heard in Masnago thus set the technical assessment of the striker alongside the memory of a person who was present in the lives of others. The celebration of the athlete belongs to the history of football; that of the man is conveyed instead through his relationships with teammates and those who sought him out. It is this dual reading, sporting and human, that explains the participation of the guests who came for Pietro Anastasi. ## The story told by the plaque
### From the national team to the provincial side
The Municipality has installed a plaque commemorating Anastasi's success in Varese and the memory Italy has preserved of him. The image of the footballer in a red-and-white shirt faces the entrance to the Franco Ossola. The message goes beyond Varese's history and also evokes what Anastasi represented for those who followed the national team and for those who had seen him star in the Italian championships.
For national-team supporters, the memory is tied to the 1968 European Championship final, played in Rome. Anastasi and Gigi Riva scored the two goals of the match. For those who had followed Varese, on the other hand, his name evoked the season of the provincial side capable of upending the league's balance, with the 5-0 victory over Juventus. Inter came after Juventus, but the bond with the red-and-white shirt remained the focal point of the dedication in front of the stadium.
### The decisive move to Varese
The plaque also speaks to those who, having emigrated from the South, looked to a footballer as an example, an idol and a reason for redemption. Anastasi, born in Catania and later raised in Varese, became a symbol for different audiences: for those who supported Italy, for those who recognized the strength of the provincial side and for those who supported the player at the big clubs.
The origins of his relationship with Varese are conveyed through Guido Borghi's account and an incident involving Alfredo Casati, a club executive. Casati was supposed to board a flight in Catania, but gave his seat on the plane to a woman who urgently needed to return to Milan. He therefore stayed in the city and took the opportunity to attend a match. Massiminiana were playing: Casati saw Anastasi and decided to bring him to Varese.
From that decision developed Pietro's deep bond with the new city, with his Anna and with so many people. The account of the transfer adds a concrete element to the ceremony: before the champion celebrated by the national team and the big clubs, there was the player seen on the pitch in Catania. Fate, as the account heard in Masnago described it, brought that match, Casati and his future experience in Varese together.
It is this sequence that completes the meaning of the square's new name. In front of the Franco Ossola, the athlete remembered for his goals, the man described as generous and the person who had built a relationship with Anna and the city came together. The applause directed at Anastasi, whether in person or in thought, accompanied a dedication born of his sporting history and his life in Varese.
*Source: [varesenews.it](https://www.varesenews.it/2026/10/se-napoli-ha-maradona-varese-ha-anastasi-il-piazzale-dello-stadio-intitolato-a-pietruzzu/2708932/)*
